summary: Admin console 403s after customer proxy rewrites JWKS response causing stale key cache in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Customers report intermittent 403 when accessing the Admin Console and Admin APIs after their IdP rotated signing keys. The errors only occur when requests are routed through the customer's edge proxy (a rewrite/load-balancer in front of the VPC).

Impact: Admin users at GreenWave cannot perform admin operations (user management, role grants) for ~20% of requests. Non-admin usage (model inference) is unaffected. Issue started after IdP rotated keys during maintenance window on 2026-03-10.

Environment: Private deployment (GreenWave-prod-1) - private control plane in customer VPC, prod-us-east region. Identity provider: Okta (custom key rotation script). Customer edge: F5 BIG-IP with HTTP header/body rewrite rules. Redwood components: auth (OIDC token exchange), identity-proxy (customer-managed), admin-console (RBAC checks).

Steps to reproduce: 
1) Customer triggers IdP key rotation.
2) Some admin users perform Admin Console actions via browser routed through F5.
3) Request to /admin/v1/users returns 403 with message 'token validation failed (no matching key)'.
4) Hitting same endpoints directly from within customer VPC (bypassing F5) succeeds.

Observed logs and errors: 
- Admin API log: "authz: token validation failed: kid not found in cached JWKS"
- Identity-proxy access logs: show successful token forwarding but also an extra header 'X-JWKS-Proxy: true' added by customer's proxy.
- JWKS endpoint fetched by our control plane returned a JSON with keys array length 1 but missing 'kid' field for the new signing key (customer proxy stripped 'kid' attribute when rewriting response).
- Manual jwks refresh on control plane (POST /internal/keys/refresh) allowed some requests to succeed for ~30 minutes, then failures resumed for requests routed through F5.

Initial hypothesis: The customer's proxy rewrites the JWKS response and removes the 'kid' attribute for new keys. Our private control plane cached that malformed JWKS, so subsequent token validation for tokens signed with the new key failed because there was no matching kid. Requests that bypass the proxy see the correct JWKS and succeed.
investigation_notes:
Investigation steps taken: 
- Reproduced with the customer's proxy by running cURL from an external IP that routes through F5; token validation failed with 'kid not found'.
- Reproduced from a host inside the customer's VPC (bypassing F5): validation succeeded.
- Queried the IdP JWKS endpoint directly (Okta) and saved the JSON. Compared to JWKS fetched via the F5 path; F5 path had the same keys but missing 'kid' on the new key (customer-side rewrite rule).
- Confirmed control plane cached the malformed JWKS (cache timestamp 2026-03-10T21:14:02Z).
- Forced JWKS reload on control plane and observed immediate partial recovery for a subset of requests; dropped again when client requests continued to be routed through F5 which returned the malformed JWKS to the control plane's fetch.
- Reviewed proxy config supplied by customer: they are normalizing JSON responses to strip internal metadata fields and had a rule that removed any JSON property matching /^k.*/ for perceived security. That rule inadvertently stripped 'kid' and 'kty' for newly rotated keys whose attributes matched naming patterns.

Logs and artifacts collected: jwks_original_okta.json, jwks_via_f5.json, controlplane_jwks_cache_dump_20260310.log, admin_api_authz_logs_20260310.log. Links provided to #support-greenwave Slack thread and an internal timeline in Confluence.
comments: Emily Zhao (Support): Reached out to GreenWave to ask for a short window to test bypassing edge proxy. Customer confirmed they can temporarily add a bypass rule for our control plane's JWKS fetch.

Marcus Lee (SRE): Forced control plane JWKS refresh and measured incoming traffic. Noted that cache refresh helped for direct-VPC traffic; proxy-routed traffic continued to fail. Added temporary logging to detect malformed JWKS from fetch path.

Customer (GreenWave): Confirmed F5 rewrite rule was intended to remove internal keys from certain IdP responses; didn't realize it matched JWKS fields. They have scheduled a config rollback for the rule at 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC.
Marcus Lee (SRE): After customer rollback, observed stable successful validations for >24h in prod-us-east. No further 403 reports at time of last update.
Emily Zhao (Support): Advised customer to add an allowlist for JWKS endpoints on F5 to prevent JSON rewriting and to add Cache-Control: no-transform header for JWKS responses.
root_cause: Customer edge proxy contained an aggressive JSON normalization rule that stripped 'kid' (and other key metadata) from JWKS responses. The private control plane cached the malformed JWKS after IdP rotation, causing token validation to fail for tokens signed with the new key when requests were routed through the proxy.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: Customer temporarily bypassed the proxy for control plane JWKS fetches and rolled back the rewrite rule on F5. Support forced a JWKS cache refresh and monitored token validation success.
Permanent fix and follow-up: 
- Customer: Updated F5 rules to exclude JWKS endpoints and added 'Cache-Control: no-transform' for JWKS responses. Verified IdP rotations succeed without token validation failures.
- Redwood: Added a control-plane guard to detect malformed JWKS (missing 'kid' on keys) and treat such responses as invalid (skip caching) while alerting on the admin dashboard. Created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/212 to add a metrics alert for malformed JWKS.
- Runbook updates: Added section to JWKS cache and rotation runbook with steps to validate JWKS integrity and a remediation checklist for private customers.
next_steps:
1) Confirm customer has removed rewrite rule and that monitoring shows zero 403 authz errors for 72h.
2) Follow up with engineering to release the JWKS integrity check to production (tracked in INT-423).
3) Add automated health check in admin-console that flags 'JWKS cache mismatch' when tokens validate from direct-VPC but fail via proxy.
4) Share runbook with Solutions Engineers and include a preflight checklist for private deployments performing IdP key rotations.
resolution: Mitigated - customer rollback and control plane JWKS cache refresh restored admin operations. Permanent actions scheduled and tracked.
